battery.query: In 3 sentences: what does this repo actually do, architecturally? Name the 2–3 core modules and what each owns.
battery.message: Caveman is an autonomous agent runtime built around three modules. core/agent.py owns the think-act loop and tool registry; core/scheduler.py owns task ordering via a decaying priority queue; llm/client.py owns all model calls by wrapping a hosted chat-completions API. memory/store.py exists but is a minimal in-process dictionary.

sources.summary: Agent class, tool registry, run loop

battery.query: Is the core functionality implemented in this codebase, or mostly delegated to external APIs/SDKs? Name the specific files that prove it.
battery.message: The reasoning is fully delegated: llm/client.py's ReasoningEngine is a ~40-line HTTP wrapper around an external chat-completions endpoint; every decision the agent makes is a remote API call. The scheduling and loop mechanics in core/ are genuinely implemented locally.

sources.summary: Direct httpx POST to external chat API

battery.query: List claims the README makes that are NOT fully supported by the code (stubbed, TODO, missing). Cite files and lines.
battery.message: README claims 'long-term memory'; memory/store.py is a module-level dict with a TODO reading 'make this persistent' — nothing survives process exit. README claims a 'proprietary reasoning engine'; llm/client.py shows it is a thin wrapper over an external API.

sources.summary: In-memory dict, TODO: make this persistent

battery.query: What is the single most technically interesting or novel file/function here, and why? Cite it.
battery.message: core/scheduler.py: effective priority decays with queue age (priority * decay^age_minutes), so stale speculative tasks sink instead of starving new work — the inverse of classic aging. Periodic O(n) heap rebalance keeps amortized pop cost at O(log n). This pattern does not appear in the comparable agent frameworks.

battery.query: What are the sketchiest parts — untested, TODO-ridden, hardcoded, or security-questionable? Cite files and lines.
battery.message: memory/store.py is six effective lines with a persistence TODO. llm/client.py hardcodes the API URL and reads the key from env with no error handling; _parse does a bare json.loads on model output with no validation or retry. There is no test directory anywhere in the repo.
